issues.description: The problem text (Part 2) states the milk method should be messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and include the milk volume in its return string, but the UML, the template usage (Main.java) and the reference solution define messageOnMilk() with no parameters (returning a String). This creates a signature mismatch: students following the textual instruction would implement a method with a double parameter, which will not match the interface/methods used in the template and tests and will lead to compilation/test failures or confusion about the correct API.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the signature mismatch by making the problem statement consistent with the UML and template: change the textual description to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and update the example return string to e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if the intention is to include milk volume, update the UML, template (Main.java) calls, and reference solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) everywhere.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a double parameter and a return string containing the volume), but both the template usage (Main.java) and the solution implement and call messageOnMilk() with no parameter. This signature mismatch between the textual requirement and the provided/template code creates confusion about the correct method name and signature students must implement and will likely cause compilation/test failures if students follow the textual description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred minimal fix: update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() (no parameters) and adjust the example return value to "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if volume must be tracked, update the template and solution to define Milkable.messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust all implementations and calls (e.g., Main.java) accordingly.
